column2: Specify the broader educational goals that students are working towards over time. These objectives often align with curriculum standards and describe the knowledge, skills, or understanding students should develop across a unit or series of lessons.

Define what students should achieve by the end of this specific lesson. These should be clear, measurable, and focused on what students will learn or be able to demonstrate within the single learning experience.

List the key subject-specific words, academic language, and important phrases that students will encounter or use during the lesson. This field supports vocabulary development and language comprehension, helping students access and express their learning.

Describe the relevant concepts, skills, or content that students have already learned and will build on in this lesson. This helps establish continuity in learning and ensures the new lesson connects meaningfully to students’ prior knowledge.

Provide an overview or step-by-step outline of how the lesson will be delivered. Include the sequence of learning activities, transitions, timings, and instructional strategies that will guide the flow of the lesson from start to finish.
